[[File:Hachioji Jinjya.JPG|250px|thumb|Hachioji Shrine at Fukazawa Mountain (Hachioji City)]]
'''Hachioji Shrine''' (八王子神社) enshrines the [[Hachioji Gongen|Eight Princes (Hachioji Gongen)]] (八柱の御子神) of [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (also known as [[Gozu Tennō|Gozu Tennō]]). It is also referred to as '''Hachioji-miya''' or '''Yahashira Shrine''' (八柱神社), and there are numerous such shrines across Japan.

== Overview ==

Hachioji Shrines originated from the syncretic belief in [[Hachioji Gongen]] under the system of [[Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]]. 

In [[913|913]], Buddhist monk Kegon Bosatsu Myōgyō had a vision of Gozu Tennō and eight princes while practicing asceticism at Fukazawa Mountain, currently [[Mount Shiroyama]] in [[Hachiōji|Hachioji City]], Tokyo. Inspired by this revelation, he enshrined [[Hachioji Gongen]] at Fukazawa Mountain in [[916|916]].

Gozu Tennō, regarded as a Buddhist guardian deity, is believed to have had eight children with [[Harisai-sho]]. These children are enshrined as the Hachioji deities.

The eight princes were later associated with eight directions and calendar deities, also known as [[Hasshōshin]]:
* [[Taisai-shin]] (Jupiter, Sōkō Tennō)
* [[Daishōgun|Daishōgun]] (Venus, Maō Tennō)
* [[Taion-shin]] (Saturn, Kumara Tennō)
* [[Saigyōshin]] (Mercury, Tokutatsu Tennō)
* [[Saiha Shin]] (Saturn, Ryōji Tennō)
* [[Saisetsujin]] (Mars, Jishin Tennō)
* [[Ōbanjin]] (Rahu, Takushin Tennō)
* [[Hyōbijin]] (Ketu, Jakidokikami Tennō)

During the [[Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]] of the Meiji era, the eight princes were redefined as the [[Five Male and Three Female Deities]], born from the [[Oath]] between [[Amaterasu]] and Susanoo:
* [[Ame-no-oshihomimi]]
* [[Ame-no-Hohi]]
* [[Amatsuhikone]]
* [[Ikutsuhikone]]
* [[Kumanokusubi]]
* [[Takiribime]]
* [[Ichikishima-hime]]
* [[Tagitsuhime]]

Certain shrines enshrine different deities. For example, at [[Yasaka Shrine|Yasaka Shrine]], the eight princes are identified as [[Yashimajinumi]], [[Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|Isotakeru-no-kami]], and other deities.

[[11]] identifies the two as such

* [[Taisaijin]] ([[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Ame-no-oshihomimi]])
* [[Taionjin]] ([[Ichikishima-hime]])
* [[Saigyōshin]] ([[Tagorihime]])
* [[Saiha Shin]] ([[Tagitsuhime]])
* [[Saisetsujin]] ([[Ame no Hohi]])
* [[Ōbanjin]] ([[Ikutsuhikone]])
* [[Hyōbijin]] ([[Kumanokusubi]])

== Origin of Hachioji City ==
The name "Hachioji City" originated during the Sengoku period when [[Hōjō Ujiteru|Hōjō Ujiteru]] named his castle [[Hachiōji Castle|Hachioji Castle]] after the legends of the eight princes.
